join_order.notes: scan company_type/kind.off+.dat (4 rows) to find target_ct_id
scan info_type/info.off+.dat (113 rows) to find target_it_id

title is driver (PK dense, id=i+1); for each surviving title scan mc rows via _idx/movie_companies__movie_id__offsets.bin between off[v] and off[v+1]; apply company_type_id == target_ct_id and NOT LIKE on note

for each surviving title id v, look up _idx/movie_info_idx__movie_id__offsets.bin range and require at least one row where info_type_id == target_it_id; bottom 10 rank is rare so this prunes heavily. Use existence check (early-exit) per title; only emit (title, mc_row) tuples when both probes survive

filters.predicate: production_year BETWEEN 2005 AND 2010 AND production_year != INT32_MIN
note NOT LIKE '%(as Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Pictures)%' AND note non-empty

data_structures.ct_target: int32_t scalar (target_ct_id) resolved at runtime; sentinel -1 if not found -> empty result
data_structures.it_target: int32_t scalar (target_it_id) resolved at runtime; sentinel -1 if not found -> empty result
data_structures.mc_movie_id_index: mmap int32_t[] offsets array from _idx/movie_companies__movie_id__offsets.bin (size = max_title_id + 2)
data_structures.aggregation: per-thread mins (best_note as offset+len, best_title as offset+len, best_year as int32), reduced at end via lexicographic compare

parallelism.notes: parallelize over title row ranges (driver). Each thread maintains local mins; final reduce picks the lexicographically minimum note/title and numeric minimum year independently (SQL MIN per column).

execution_notes: Resolve target_ct_id and target_it_id first; if either is -1, return NULL row immediately.
Drive on title (dense PK; id = row_index + 1). Year filter is cheap and reduces probe count by ~12x.

For each surviving title v: walk mc range [off_mc[v], off_mc[v+1]); evaluate company_type_id and NOT LIKE; if at least one mc row survives, check mi_idx range for any row with info_type_id == target_it_id (early exit).

Because 'bottom 10 rank' is very rare, the mi_idx existence check eliminates nearly all titles. Consider checking mi_idx existence FIRST per title before the mc scan to save work — but mc scan is needed anyway to emit mc.note for MIN. Order: title-year -> mi_idx existence (early prune) -> mc scan -> note/company filter.
MIN aggregation: compare varlen by lexicographic byte order; treat empty (NULL) as not eligible for MIN.
NOT LIKE: use memmem on note slice; if note is empty (NULL) treat row as failing per guide.
Three independent MINs: track separately; do NOT couple them to the same row.
